raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Fixes #61150. With `vllm::moe_forward` or `vllm::moe_forward_shared` in `splitting_ops` under PIECEWISE CUDA graphs, decode output turns to garbage after the first token (` Par Par Par ...`). With `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG`, the `CUDAGraphWrapper` replay address check fails. This PR makes the split MoE op write into an output buffer that is allocated in the captured piece before it, the same way attention works. The piece after the op then reads a fixed address on replay.

Compared with #61179, this fix:

- Keeps the user's `splitting_ops` as written. [61179](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61179) renames the MoE ops in it to new ops, so the existing `test_moe_splitting_ops_deepep_ht_inductor_partition` fails on [61179](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61179) unless the test is edited. That test passes here unchanged.
- Is much smaller outside `tests/`: +47/-9 in `moe_runner.py` only, with no new ops. [61179](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61179) adds about 180 lines across `moe_runner.py` and `compilation.py`, including two new registered ops.
- Tests all three broken paths: `moe_forward` with the FX split, `moe_forward` with Inductor graph partition, and `moe_forward_shared`. The GPU test in [61179](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61179) covers only `moe_forward` with the FX split.

## Claims

- With the MoE ops in `splitting_ops` under PIECEWISE, output now matches the default split and eager. Before, it was garbage after the first token.
- The DEBUG replay input-address assertion no longer fires.
- `moe_forward_shared` and the Inductor graph partition path had the same bug, and the same change fixes them.
- When the MoE op is not in `splitting_ops` (the default), the bare op is still called, with no extra buffer or copy.

## Validation

Setup: 1x NVIDIA RTX 6000 Ada. vLLM `0.31.1rc1.dev296+gfe4df3df0` (commit `fe4df3df0eb7`), torch 2.13.0+cu130, triton 3.7.1. Model `ibm-granite/granite-3.0-1b-a400m-instruct`. The logs show `FLASH_ATTN`, `TritonExperts` MoE backend, `PIECEWISE`, capture sizes `[1, 2, 4, 8, 16]`.

Reproducer: the `split_repro.py` script from the issue, unchanged:

```
python split_repro.py --out ./split_repro_out
```

It runs each arm in its own process: greedy decoding, 32 tokens, rounds of batch 4 / 2 / 4, prefix caching on, V1 model runner. `split` adds the two MoE ops to the default `splitting_ops`. `split_nograph` is `split` with capture sizes `[1]`, so no graph is replayed. `split_debug` is `split` with DEBUG logging.

Before (unpatched, 3 runs; runs 2 and 3 ran only `default` and `split`). `split` matched `default` in 0 of 10 completions in every run:

```
eager          rc=0 address_assert=False vs eager - vs default 10/10
default        rc=0 address_assert=False vs eager 10/10 vs default -
split          rc=0 address_assert=False vs eager 0/10 vs default 0/10
split_nograph  rc=0 address_assert=False vs eager 10/10 vs default 10/10
split_debug    rc=1 address_assert=True vs eager - vs default -
```

`split_debug` failed with `AssertionError: Input addresses for cudagraphs are different during replay`.

After (with this PR, 6 runs, all five arms). Every run printed:

```
eager          rc=0 address_assert=False vs eager - vs default 10/10
default        rc=0 address_assert=False vs eager 10/10 vs default -
split          rc=0 address_assert=False vs eager 10/10 vs default 10/10
split_nograph  rc=0 address_assert=False vs eager 10/10 vs default 10/10
split_debug    rc=0 address_assert=False vs eager 10/10 vs default 10/10
```

In 3 of these runs I also compared the JSON outputs. `split` (graphs replayed) has the same tokens and the same top-1 logprobs as `split_nograph` (no replay) in 10 of 10 completions, bit for bit. With the script's `--offload` flag (prefetch CPU offloader on experts, which the issue also lists), `split` and `split_debug` matched `default` 10/10 with no assertion (1 run).

New tests in `tests/compile/fullgraph/test_moe_splitting_ops.py`:

```
pytest -v -s tests/compile/fullgraph/test_moe_splitting_ops.py
```

- `test_moe_forward_as_splitting_op[False]` and `[True]`: granite, PIECEWISE, default `splitting_ops` against the MoE ops added, compared with `check_logprobs_close`. `[True]` uses Inductor graph partition.
- `test_moe_forward_shared_as_splitting_op`: `Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B` config shrunk to 4 layers, with dummy weights. Its runner has shared experts. DEBUG logging turns on the replay address assertion in `CUDAGraphWrapper`.

On the unpatched `moe_runner.py`: 3 failed (garbage text in the two granite tests, the address assertion in the shared test). With this PR: 3 passed, in 2 runs. CI picks up the file through the existing `compile/fullgraph` step in `.buildkite/test_areas/pytorch.yaml`.

Other checks:

- Configs that already worked give the same tokens and top-1 logprobs as the unpatched code, bit for bit. This was checked for both ops, with the default model runner (V2). It covers the default config with no split, `enforce_eager` with the MoE ops split, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE with the MoE ops split, and the Transformers backend.
- PIECEWISE with the MoE ops split, under `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`: no sync error.
- `tests/kernels/moe/test_shared_fused_moe_routed_transform.py`, `test_zero_expert_moe.py`, `test_moe_layer.py` (EP/DP cases deselected): no failures.
- `tests/compile/test_config.py`: 64 passed with and without this PR. In both cases the same 25 tests failed, all because `facebook/opt-125m` could not be downloaded in my environment.
- `pre-commit` passes on the changed files.

## Details

Root cause: when a MoE op is a splitting op, it runs eagerly between two captured pieces. It returns a tensor that the MoE kernel allocates fresh on every call. That tensor comes from the caching allocator, not from the graph pool. `CUDAGraphWrapper` does not copy inputs into static buffers, so the next piece reads its input from the address it had at capture time. On replay the op returns a tensor at a new address, and the piece reads freed or reused memory. Debug prints confirmed this. At capture, `moe_forward` returned one address, and the next piece (`submod_4`) recorded it as its input. At replay, `moe_forward` returned another address, and the replay check reported that address for `submod_4`. The MoE input address did not change. Attention does not have this problem: its output buffer is allocated in traced code, and the op writes into it. `breakable_cudagraph.py` states the same rule for eager segments.

Fix (only `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py`):

- `moe_forward` gets an optional `output` argument. `moe_forward_shared` gets optional `shared_output` and `fused_output` arguments. All are declared in `mutates_args`. When they are given, the op copies its result into them.
- `MoERunner._select_forward` checks whether the op is in `compilation_config.splitting_ops`, with or without `.default`, like `should_split`. If it is, the runner calls a small wrapper. The wrapper allocates the buffers in traced code with the op's own fake function and passes them to the op. The buffer then lives in the captured piece before the op, so its address stays fixed for each batch size.
- Otherwise the bare op is called as before. The TPU and CPU paths are unchanged.
- The change is in the MoE layer, not in a model runner, so both runners get it. The reproducer ran on V1. The new tests and the regression checks ran on V2.

Tradeoffs and limits:

- With the MoE op split, each MoE layer does one extra allocation and one device-to-device copy of its output.
- `moe_forward_shared` now declares `mutates_args`, so on the default path it goes through `auto_functionalized`. Output is the same as before, bit for bit, but I did not measure default-path throughput.
- The Inductor partition path for `moe_forward_shared` uses the same code but has no test. In that config the shared test saw no `CUDAGraphWrapper` capture or replay, so the address check could not catch anything.
- I did not run a shared-experts model with real weights. That path is checked only by the dummy-weight test.
- `vllm::transformers_moe_forward` (Transformers backend) also returns a fresh tensor. If a user adds it to `splitting_ops` under PIECEWISE, output is still garbage with this PR (0/10). It is a separate op and is not changed here.
- `test_moe_forward_as_splitting_op[False]` prints a `UserWarning` for one prompt at token 25, and `check_logprobs_close` accepts it. The same change appears with no graph replay at all (capture sizes `[1]`), so it comes from where the graph is cut, not from this bug.
- The older comment above `_moe_forward` says these functions only pass control along. It is now slightly out of date, because they also copy into the given buffers.

---

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+import pytest
+
+from tests.models.utils import check_logprobs_close
+from vllm.config import CompilationConfig, CUDAGraphMode, LoggingConfig
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+PROMPTS = [
+    "The capital of France is",
+    "Write a haiku about the sea:",
+    "List three prime numbers greater than 100:",
+    "Q: What is 17 times 23?\nA:",
+]
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(not current_platform.is_cuda(), reason="needs CUDA")
+
+
+def _compilation_config(splitting_ops, use_inductor_graph_partition):
+    return CompilationConfig(
+        cudagraph_mode=CUDAGraphMode.PIECEWISE,
+        splitting_ops=splitting_ops,
+        use_inductor_graph_partition=use_inductor_graph_partition,
+    )
+
+
+def _moe_splitting_ops(use_inductor_graph_partition):
+    splitting_ops = list(CompilationConfig._attention_ops)
+    if not use_inductor_graph_partition:
+        # Only added by default when splitting_ops is None.
+        splitting_ops += [
+            "vllm::unified_kv_cache_update",
+            "vllm::unified_mla_kv_cache_update",
+        ]
+    return splitting_ops + ["vllm::moe_forward", "vllm::moe_forward_shared"]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("use_inductor_graph_partition", [False, True])
+def test_moe_forward_as_splitting_op(vllm_runner, use_inductor_graph_partition):
+    """A splitting op runs outside the captured pieces, so the piece after
+    `vllm::moe_forward` must not read the MoE output from the address it had
+    at capture time (#61150)."""
+    outputs = []
+    for splitting_ops in (None, _moe_splitting_ops(use_inductor_graph_partition)):
+        with vllm_runner(
+            "ibm-granite/granite-3.0-1b-a400m-instruct",
+            max_model_len=1024,
+            compilation_config=_compilation_config(
+                splitting_ops, use_inductor_graph_partition
+            ),
+        ) as llm:
+            outputs.append(
+                llm.generate_greedy_logprobs(PROMPTS, max_tokens=32, num_logprobs=5)
+            )
+    check_logprobs_close(
+        outputs_0_lst=outputs[0],
+        outputs_1_lst=outputs[1],
+        name_0="default_splitting_ops",
+        name_1="moe_splitting_ops",
+    )
+
+
+def _shrink_qwen3_5_moe(hf_config):
+    hf_config.get_text_config().update(
+        {
+            "num_hidden_layers": 4,
+            "layer_types": ["linear_attention"] * 3 + ["full_attention"],
+            "num_experts": 16,
+            "num_experts_per_tok": 4,
+            "mtp_num_hidden_layers": 0,
+        }
+    )
+    return hf_config
+
+
+def test_moe_forward_shared_as_splitting_op(vllm_runner):
+    """Same as above for `vllm::moe_forward_shared`. With DEBUG logging,
+    CUDAGraphWrapper asserts that replayed inputs keep their capture
+    addresses, so dummy weights are enough."""
+    with vllm_runner(
+        "Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B",
+        load_format="dummy",
+        hf_overrides=_shrink_qwen3_5_moe,
+        max_model_len=1024,
+        enable_chunked_prefill=None,
+        limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 0, "video": 0},
+        logging_config=LoggingConfig(log_level="DEBUG"),
+        compilation_config=_compilation_config(_moe_splitting_ops(False), False),
+    ) as llm:
+        llm.generate_greedy(PROMPTS, max_tokens=8)
